footer: Fictional organization. Synthetic evidence. Demonstration use only. No customer or production environment is represented.

pages.title: Executive assessment summary
pages.subtitle: From technical findings to business risk and validated remediation.
items: The synthetic environment shows common weaknesses affecting management-plane protection, network segmentation, privileged access and security visibility. The highest concern is the combination of broad reachability, privileged exposure and incomplete monitoring.

A compromised user endpoint could create a path toward privileged network control. Excessive east-west access also increases lateral-movement potential, while incomplete logging can reduce detection and investigation capability.
The sample demonstrates how WeOwnIT connects evidence, business impact, remediation ownership, validation criteria and residual risk - rather than stopping at a list of findings.

pages.title: Business context & critical assets
pages.subtitle: Security decisions start with what the business depends on.
items: ACME Manufacturing is a fictional 250-user organization with HQ, two branches, business-critical ERP, internal application services, remote connectivity and centralized security management.
Internet edge firewall; management network; ERP and application servers; branch VPN connectivity; centralized logging; administrative identities.
Protect availability of connectivity, integrity of privileged configuration, confidentiality of business data, segmentation between trust zones and accountability of administrative actions.

pages.title: Scope, assumptions & methodology
pages.subtitle: A repeatable assessment model for risk-informed engineering.
items: Architecture, trust boundaries, administrative exposure, segmentation, firewall policy, logging, privileged access, backup and recovery readiness.
CONTEXT -> ASSESS -> ANALYZE -> PRIORITIZE -> REMEDIATE -> VALIDATE -> PROVE
This sample uses SYNTHETIC / INFERRED evidence. In a client engagement, evidence is classified as Confirmed, Observed, Inferred or Not Tested.

pages.title: Architecture & trust boundaries
pages.subtitle: Where lower-trust zones can reach privileged control.
items: Internet / User / Server / Management / Security Management / Branch VPN
The synthetic User zone can reach administrative HTTPS/SSH on the edge firewall. That creates an unnecessary attack path from a lower-trust workstation segment to a privileged security control.
Administrative access originates only from the management zone or approved remote-admin path, protected by MFA, named accounts, least privilege and centralized logging.

pages.title: F-001 - Management plane reachable from User zone
pages.subtitle: Detailed finding - HIGH
items: Administrative HTTPS and SSH services are reachable from the general corporate user network.

A compromised endpoint could establish connectivity to the firewall management plane. Combined with credential compromise or another authentication weakness, this creates a path toward privileged control.
Unauthorized policy changes, VPN manipulation, routing changes, security-control bypass, logging modification and service disruption.

pages.title: F-001 - Control strategy & validation
pages.subtitle: Prevent, limit, detect, recover - then prove.
items: Dedicated management network; trusted administrative sources; MFA; named administrator accounts.
Role-based administrator profiles; least privilege; restricted management protocols.
Administrative login logging; failed-authentication monitoring; configuration-change logging.
Validated configuration backup and documented recovery path.
MEDIUM - changing management access without confirming alternate connectivity can cause administrative lockout. Validate console/OOB access first.
MGMT -> HTTPS ALLOW; USER -> HTTPS BLOCK; WAN -> SSH BLOCK; MFA VERIFIED; admin events visible in central logs.
LOW, provided that access sources, MFA, named accounts and centralized logging are verified.

pages.title: F-002 - Excessive east-west network access
pages.subtitle: Detailed finding - HIGH
items: A broad User-to-Server security policy permits more services than required for business operation.
A compromised workstation may obtain unnecessary reachability toward internal workloads, increasing lateral-movement opportunities.
USER -> APP : required business services only; USER -> DB/MGMT : denied unless explicitly justified.
Positive test for required application flow plus negative tests for database and management ports. Review logs for denied non-business traffic.
MEDIUM after least-privilege policy and monitoring, subject to application dependencies and approved exceptions.

pages.title: Remediation roadmap & closure evidence
pages.subtitle: Turn findings into owned, measurable work.
items: F-001 management exposure - Network Security - low effort / medium change risk.
F-002 policy reduction - Network Security + Application Owner - medium effort / medium change risk. Enforce MFA for privileged accounts.
Centralize security logging and verify administrative event coverage. Validate backup/recovery procedure.
OPEN -> REMEDIATION PLANNED -> IMPLEMENTED -> VALIDATION REQUIRED -> VERIFIED -> CLOSED.
Configuration evidence, approved change record, positive/negative tests, log proof, residual-risk statement and owner acceptance.
Executive summary + technical findings + remediation backlog + target architecture + validation plan + reusable evidence.
